info.title: Hodei-Shield API
info.summary: Third-party risk and compliance posture, for your own systems.
info.description:
## Versioning

`/v1` is frozen. These changes are **compatible** and will happen inside it
without notice:

- a new operation;
- a new **optional** query parameter;
- a new field in a response object;
- a new value in a field documented as an open vocabulary (`status`,
  `severity`, `evidence_type`, the keys of `by_status`);
- a new `error.code`, always with the HTTP status its siblings already use;
- anything under `error.details`, which is diagnostic and not part of the
  contract — except `error.details.code` and the keys the error table of
  the operation names (`missing`, `licence`, `parameter`, `scope`,
  `limit`, `window_seconds`, `retry_after_seconds`, `status`,
  `formats`, `limit_bytes`): those are contract.
  `error.details.code` is an OPEN vocabulary: a value, once published, keeps
  its meaning and the HTTP status it is sent with; new values may be added.

Write your client so those do not break it: ignore unknown fields, do not
switch exhaustively on a documented-open vocabulary, and treat an unknown
`error.code` as "an error of this HTTP status".

These changes are **incompatible** and will NOT happen inside `/v1`. They go
to `/v2`, and `/v1` keeps serving:

- removing or renaming an operation, a parameter or a field;
- changing the type, the unit or the meaning of a field;
- making an optional parameter required, or narrowing what one accepts;
- changing which scope an operation requires;
- changing the HTTP status an existing `error.code` is sent with.

## Reads and writes

Every operation that reads is a `GET`. Three kinds of operation change state,
each a `POST`: the key writes, `POST /v1/alerts/{id}/acknowledge` and
`POST /v1/alerts/{id}/resolve` under the write scope `alerts:write`, and
`POST /v1/risks/{id}/transition` under `risks:write`;
`POST /v1/act/proposals` (`createActProposal`), which only RECORDS a proposal
that a person of the tenant approves before anything changes,
reachable only with a user's OAuth access token issued for the HodeiShield MCP
server that carries `act:propose`; and a person's decision on such a proposal,
`POST /v1/act/proposals/{id}/approve` and `…/reject`, reachable only with a
user's OAuth access token of the HodeiShield CLI that carries `act:decide` and
whose sign-in was confirmed within the last 15 minutes (**403**
`STEP_UP_REQUIRED` otherwise; the same window applies to the list of proposals
waiting for the caller, `GET /v1/act/inbox`). An approval does not execute the action: it is
executed in the console within the approval window. Any other method on a path that exists
answers **405** with `Allow` naming the one method it serves, and on a path that
does not exist answers **404**: neither changes any state. A new write is offered
only as a new operation, which is a compatible change.

The alert writes are authorised by an API key and its scope alone, with no interactive
confirmation, because the caller is an automation (a SOAR): a **tenant API key**
in its own tenant, or an MSSP **portfolio key** in the client tenant it names
with `X-HS-Tenant`, exactly as on the reads (a tenant outside its client set
answers **404** `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`). The tenant's IP allowlist (`IP_NOT_ALLOWED`;
for a portfolio key, that same 404) and the module of the scope (`supply_risk`
for `alerts:write` and `risks:write`, else `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`) apply to a
write exactly as to a read. An OAuth access token cannot make them. No read
scope implies a write scope, a write scope implies no read scope, existing
keys do not hold one, and only a user whose role may make the same change in the
console can grant it: `alerts:write` a role that may close alerts,
`risks:write` an administrator role of the tenant (on a portfolio key, an
organisation administrator of the provider, for both). The key acts with the role of the **user
who created it**, read on every request: a creator who was demoted, suspended,
deleted or removed from the tenant (for a portfolio key: from the provider, or
no longer reaching that client) takes the power away from the key (**403**,
`WRITE_ACTOR_UNRESOLVED` or `ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED`). The console's
role-by-severity rule applies: an MSSP analyst's key closes medium and low
alerts only; and a risk moves only along the lifecycle the console allows
(**409** `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` otherwise). A write takes a JSON object body (an unknown key is a **400**), is
refused while the licence is in its grace period (**403** `LICENCE_INACTIVE`),
and is idempotent: repeating a change already made answers the current state with
`changed: false`, while a concurrent change between its read and its write
answers **409** (`ALERT_STATE_CHANGED`). Every change writes one entry in the
tenant's audit trail with the key id, the acting user, the old and new status and
the reason.

## Downloads

An operation whose success is a FILE (`GET /v1/reports/{id}/download`) answers
**200** with the bytes, the `Content-Type` of the format asked for and
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="…"`; it never answers a URL to fetch
them from. Its errors are the same JSON envelope as everywhere else. A file that
cannot be served as asked is a **409** with `error.details.code`: the report is
not ready yet (`REPORT_NOT_READY`), its content has no renderer for that format
(`FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`) or the file exceeds the size the operation serves
(`FILE_TOO_LARGE`, with `limit_bytes`). Every file delivered is recorded in the
tenant's audit trail with the credential that received it.

## Authentication

Every operation takes `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. Three credentials
exist:

- a **tenant API key** (`hsk_…`): belongs to ONE tenant and carries an
  explicit list of scopes; it can read nothing outside that tenant, whatever it
  asks for. It can hold the write scopes `alerts:write` and `risks:write`;
- a user's **OAuth access token** (`hs_at_…`): one user, ONE tenant chosen
  at consent, read scopes only — plus, for a token issued for the HodeiShield
  MCP server, the OAuth-only `act:propose`, which lets it record proposals
  (`createActProposal`) and read their status (`getActProposal`); and, for a
  token of the HodeiShield CLI, the OAuth-only `act:decide`, which lets the
  person list the proposals waiting for a decision and approve or reject them;
- an MSSP **portfolio key** (`hsp_…`): held by a managed security service
  provider, it reads ANY of its client tenants, ONE per request, selected with
  the request header `X-HS-Tenant: <tenant id>` (a UUID, never a slug).
  `GET /v1/portfolio/tenants` lists the tenants it may select. Read scopes,
  plus at most the write scopes `alerts:write` and `risks:write`, with a mandatory expiry. A
  tenant outside the key's portfolio answers **404**
  (`error.details.code: "TENANT_NOT_FOUND"`), exactly as one that does not
  exist.

Every successful (2xx) answer of a data operation carries `X-HS-Tenant` with
the id of the tenant whose data the body holds, for every credential; no error
carries it. A tenant API key or OAuth token may send `X-HS-Tenant` only with
its own tenant's id; any other value is a **400**
(`TENANT_SELECTOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`).

Each operation below declares the scope it requires. A credential that
authenticates but lacks the scope is answered **403**
(`error.details.code: "INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE"`), never 404: you are told what you
are missing, not that the resource does not exist.

A scope is not enough on its own: the module it names (`supply_risk`,
`compliance.nis2`, `endpoints`, …) must also be active for the tenant read
— the credential's own, or the one a portfolio key selected — at the time of the
request; a compliance framework (`compliance.<framework>`) must also be
activated for the tenant, as in the console. When it is not (the plan changed,
the module was turned off, or the framework was never activated) the
answer is **403** with `error.details.code: "MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED"`,
`error.details.scopes` naming the scopes concerned and `error.details.modules`
the modules the tenant lacks, for every credential; when the module is in the
plan but a compliance framework is not activated, `error.details.frameworks`
names those frameworks (`nis2`, …). A new key does not help; the module has to
be active again.

## Errors

Every error has the same body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "forbidden", "message": "…", "request_id": "…" } }
```

Branch on `code`, log `request_id`, show `message` to nobody but yourself.
`request_id` is also the `X-Request-Id` response header, and it is what
support will ask you for.

## Rate limits

Every response that got past authentication carries the limit that is closest
to being exhausted:

- `RateLimit-Limit` — requests allowed in the window;
- `RateLimit-Remaining` — requests left in the current window;
- `RateLimit-Reset` — **seconds** until the window renews;
- `RateLimit-Policy` — `<limit>;w=<window seconds>`.

Three limits apply, each per one-minute window: per API key, per organisation
(all of its keys together) and per service. The first two come from the licence
of the organisation the key belongs to: a higher licence tier has more room, and
an MSSP partner has more than a direct customer of the same tier. Read the
current limit from `RateLimit-Limit` and `RateLimit-Policy` rather than
hard-coding it. When one is exhausted the answer is
**429** with `error.code: "rate_limited"`, `Retry-After` (seconds) and
`error.details.scope` (`key`, `tenant` or `service`) saying which. A
write is not counted in those: it has its own budget per key (`write_key`),
plus the service ceiling, so reads and writes never spend each other's room. A
portfolio key is limited per key (`portfolio_key`), per provider across all
its portfolio keys (`portfolio_org`) and per service; once the selected tenant
is known to be in its portfolio, the client tenant's own limit (`tenant`) and
the provider's share of it (`portfolio_tenant`) apply too. Your
organisation's usage never counts against another's. Windows are fixed, so a
client can burst up to twice the limit across a window boundary: back off on
`Retry-After` rather than pacing to the second. The limits are part of the
service, not of the frozen contract: they may be raised without notice.

## Pagination, filtering and ordering

Every collection takes `page` and `per_page` (max 200) and answers with a
`pagination` object carrying `total` and `total_pages`. Every collection
takes `sort` (an enum of the fields THAT collection can order by) and
`order` (`asc`/`desc`, default `desc`). Filters are exact matches unless
the parameter says otherwise. A parameter or field with a known vocabulary lists
it in `x-hs-known-values` (an OpenAPI extension, not a JSON Schema `enum`: the
server still accepts what it accepted before; a value outside the list is served as sent and flagged by `meta.warnings` and the `X-HS-Unknown-Filter` header). Values retired from a parameter
are listed in `x-hs-deprecated-values`, with the date until which the server is
documented to accept them in `x-hs-deprecated-values-sunset`. A 2xx answer to a
request that uses one carries `Deprecation: @<unix seconds>` (RFC 9745, the day it was
announced), `Sunset: <HTTP-date>` (RFC 8594) and `Link: <…>; rel="deprecation"`, the
deprecation policy; an answer to a request that uses none carries none of them.

## Contract changes

Corrections and additions to the published contract, newest first. They ship
with the contract version (`info.version`) named in each entry. Detect a
capability by the operation, not by this string: the portfolio contract is
present when `GET /v1` lists `listPortfolioTenants`.

- **2026-11-19 — addition: incidents, AI systems, risk transitions and decisions.**
  This version carries both sets of additions listed below under 2026-11-18 and
  2026-11-17, which were drafted on separate lanes and are published together under
  this one version: the incident and AI-system register reads, the risk transition,
  and a person's decisions on ACT proposals. Nothing else changed.
- **2026-11-18 — addition: move a risk, and decide proposals as a person.**
  `POST /v1/risks/{id}/transition` (`transitionRisk`) moves a risk-register entry
  along the lifecycle the console allows, under the new key write scope
  `risks:write` (a tenant API key, or an MSSP portfolio key naming the client with
  `X-HS-Tenant`), acting with the live role of the key's creator, who must be an
  administrator of the tenant; it answers `{ data, changed }` with the entry's
  state, never its content. `GET /v1/act/inbox` (`listPendingActProposals`) lists
  the proposals waiting for a decision, and `POST /v1/act/proposals/{id}/approve`
  (`approveActProposal`) and `POST /v1/act/proposals/{id}/reject`
  (`rejectActProposal`) decide one, with a required reason, under the console's
  rules (role per action class, module, four-eyes, expiry, pause). They take only a
  user access token of the HodeiShield CLI carrying the new OAuth-only scope
  `act:decide` (every other credential: 403 `CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED`), and a
  decision needs a sign-in confirmed within the last 15 minutes. New detail codes:
  `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `OWN_PROPOSAL` (403), `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED`,
  `PROPOSAL_EXPIRED`, `ALREADY_DECIDED`, `NOT_DECIDABLE` (409); the existing
  `ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED` and `ACTIONS_PAUSED` are reused with their meaning; new 429
  `details.scope` value `decision_user`. The 409 description of the key writes now
  says "resource" instead of "alert". Nothing existing was removed, renamed or
  re-statused.
- **2026-11-17 — addition: incidents and AI systems.** Four read operations.
  `GET /v1/incidents` (`listIncidents`) and `GET /v1/incidents/{id}`
  (`getIncident`) return the tenant's incident register: type, severity, status, the
  key dates and, per incident, `notifications`, its regulatory notification deadlines
  (DORA, NIS2, GDPR, AI Act) with their stage, live status, due date and the date the
  report that met each one was submitted. `GET /v1/ai-systems` (`listAiSystems`) and
  `GET /v1/ai-systems/{id}` (`getAiSystem`) return the tenant's register of AI systems:
  risk class, lifecycle status, kind, owning unit, provider and data categories (no AI Act
  role and no review date per system: the register does not record them). Exact
  filters (`status`, `severity`, `type`; `risk_class`, `lifecycle_status`,
  `vendor_id`) with `x-hs-known-values`, `sort`, `order`, `page` and `per_page`
  (at most 200). Two new read scopes, `incidents:read` (served while the tenant has the
  `supply_risk` module) and `ai_systems:read` (served while it has `ai_governance`);
  otherwise **403** `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED` naming that module. No existing key or token
  holds them: a credential must be created, or a sign-in made, that asks for them. Free
  text other than the title and the people involved are not published. Nothing existing
  was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-15 — correction: API access is a plan feature.** API and CLI access
  belong to the plans from Comply up (Comply, Assure, Scale, Essentials, Automate,
  Operate, Enterprise) and to the trial; Respond, Free, Supplier and AI Governance
  have none. A tenant API key (`hsk_…`) or an OAuth access token not issued for
  the HodeiShield MCP server, whose tenant is on a plan without API access, was
  served; it is now refused on every request, reads and the alert writes
  (`acknowledgeAlert`, `resolveAlert`) alike, with status **403**, `error.code`
  `forbidden`, `error.details.code` `PLAN_WITHOUT_API` and
  `error.details.deniedReason` `plan_without_api`. A key that already exists is
  refused the same way, from the first request after its tenant moves to such a
  plan. A portfolio key is judged on the plan of the client tenant it selects, with
  the same answer. The plan is the effective one: a running beta counts. Re-authenticating
  does not change this; the plan can be changed in the console. The owner of each refused
  key is told once by email. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-15 — addition: proposals a person approves (`act:propose`).** A write of
  another kind: `POST /v1/act/proposals` (`createActProposal`) records a proposal of one
  action class (`create_task`, `schedule_vendor_scan`, `request_vendor_evidence`)
  that a person of the tenant approves in the console, which executes it with the
  approver's role; `GET /v1/act/proposals/{id}` (`getActProposal`) reports its
  status to the grant that made it, never its payload or approver. Both are reachable
  only with a user's OAuth access token issued for the HodeiShield MCP server that
  carries the new OAuth-only scope `act:propose` (never a tenant or portfolio key:
  403 `CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED`). New detail codes: `CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED` (403),
  `BODY_NOT_JSON`, `BODY_TOO_LARGE`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `DUPLICATE`,
  `OPEN_PROPOSAL_CAP`, `ACTIONS_PAUSED` (409); two new 429 `details.scope` values,
  `proposal_grant` (10 proposals per minute per grant) and `proposal_user` (10 per
  minute per user across all their applications). Every other path still
  answers 405 to a write. Also in this version: a 2xx answer to a request that uses a
  deprecated parameter value now carries the response headers `Deprecation` (RFC 9745),
  `Sunset` (RFC 8594) and `Link` with `rel="deprecation"`; today only the Spanish
  `severity` values of `GET /v1/alerts` (announced 2026-10-16, sunset 2027-01-14), which
  are still accepted. A request that uses none gets none. Nothing existing was removed,
  renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-15 — addition: `credential.expires_at` on `GET /v1/me`.** The
  credential block gains `expires_at`, an RFC 3339 UTC instant or null: when a tenant
  API key stops working, so an integration can warn before the key does. It is null for a
  key with no expiry, for an OAuth access token (renewed by its refresh token) and, for
  now, for a portfolio key (not reported). The key itself answers 401 from that instant.
  A compatible addition: a new key in a response object. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-15 — correction: an unknown query parameter name is refused.** A query
  parameter whose NAME the operation does not declare (`GET /v1/alerts?stauts=open`)
  was ignored and the request was served unfiltered, so a connector with a typo
  ingested the whole table believing it had filtered. It is now refused with status
  **400**, `error.code` `invalid_request` and `error.details.code`
  `UNKNOWN_QUERY_PARAMETER`; `error.details.unknown` lists the names that are not
  declared (at most 10, each cut to 64 characters; `error.details.unknown_omitted`
  counts the rest) and `error.details.allowed` the names the operation accepts. An operation
  without query parameters accepts none. A misspelt VALUE is unchanged (served as sent
  and flagged). Nothing was removed, renamed or re-statused: a request that only
  uses the declared names is unaffected.

- **2026-11-15 — correction: a key dies with its creator's role, and keys
  expire.** A tenant API key (`hsk_…`) and a portfolio key (`hsp_…`) kept
  working after the administrator who created it was removed, deactivated or
  demoted. Such a key is now refused with status **401**, the answer a revoked or
  expired key already got, unless another administrator of the tenant took the
  tenant API key over before the change. Every tenant API key now has an expiry of
  at most 365 days (`never` is no longer offered; a key that had none was given
  one and its creator was told), and a portfolio key lives at most 90 days. The
  descriptions of both security schemes say so. Re-authenticating does not help:
  an administrator of the tenant creates a new key. Nothing existing was removed,
  renamed or re-statused.
- **2026-11-14 — addition: acknowledge and resolve an alert (the first writes).**
  `POST /v1/alerts/{id}/acknowledge` (`acknowledgeAlert`) and
  `POST /v1/alerts/{id}/resolve` (`resolveAlert`, a `reason` is required),
  under the new write scope `alerts:write`, for a tenant API key or an MSSP
  portfolio key (the client named with `X-HS-Tenant`). Both answer
  `{ data, changed }`: the alert's state after the request (`status`, the
  timestamps, `resolution_reason`; never its content) and whether this request
  changed it. New `error.details.code` values: `ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED` and
  `WRITE_ACTOR_UNRESOLVED` (403), `ALERT_RESOLVED` and
  `ALERT_STATE_CHANGED` (409); new 429 `error.details.scope` value
  `write_key`. See "Reads and writes". Nothing existing changed: every read
  operation is still a `GET` and needs no new scope.
- **2026-11-14 — addition: MITRE ATT&CK techniques on alerts.**
  `GET /v1/alerts` and `GET /v1/alerts/{id}` gain two keys on the alert
  object. `mitre_techniques` lists the techniques the CTID KEV mappings assign
  to the alert's CVE (`id`, `name`, `tactic_id`, `tactic_name`,
  `subtechnique_id`; one entry per technique and tactic). `mitre_mapping`
  says why the list holds what it holds: `status` is `mapped`, `unmapped`
  (an empty list and the note «sin mapeo»: a CVE outside the CISA KEV set, or an
  alert that is not a CVE), `not_in_plan` or `unavailable`, and `source`
  names the mapping dataset, its version, the ATT&CK release and the upstream
  commit. The mapping is a feature of the tenant's plan
  (`supply_chain.mitre_mapping`): without it `mitre_techniques` is `null` and
  `status` is `not_in_plan`, and the alert is otherwise served in full (no 403).
  Treat `null` as "not served", never as "no mapping". Nothing existing was
  removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-12 — correction: the tenant's IP allowlist applies to API keys.** A
  tenant that configured an IP allowlist in the console had it enforced on console
  sessions and OAuth access tokens, but a tenant API key (`hsk_…`) was served from
  any address. A key is now refused from an address outside its tenant's
  allowlist with status **403**, `error.code` `forbidden` and
  `error.details.code` `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, the answer an OAuth access token already
  got for the same reason. A portfolio key acting in a client tenant that has an
  allowlist is refused from an address outside it with the same **404**
  `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` as a tenant outside its portfolio, so the allowlist reveals
  nothing about which tenants belong to the portfolio. The address is the one the
  client connects from. A tenant without an allowlist is unaffected.
  Re-authenticating does not help: the tenant's administrator adds the address to
  the allowlist. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-12 — correction: the portfolio listing and `/v1/me` respect each client's IP
  allowlist.** `GET /v1/portfolio/tenants` listed every client of the portfolio, and
  `GET /v1/me` counted them, from any address. A client tenant that has an IP allowlist
  excluding the address of the request is now left out of the listing and out of the count,
  with no sign that it exists; a client without an allowlist is unaffected. If a client's allowlist cannot be read, both answer **503** `service_unavailable` instead of a shorter list. Nothing existing
  was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-11-12 — correction: `MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED` is published.** An OAuth
  access token (the CLI, an MCP client) of an account without a second factor,
  used against a tenant that requires one, has always been refused with status
  **403**, `error.code` `forbidden` and `error.details.code`
  `MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED`, but the contract did not list that code among the
  detail codes every operation shares. It is listed now. Re-authenticating does
  not help: the account enrols a second factor in the console. Nothing existing
  was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-29 — addition: a warning when a filter value is not a published one.**
  `GET /v1/alerts` `severity`, `GET /v1/risks` `domain` and `status` and
  `GET /v1/compliance/controls` `status` match exactly, so a mistyped value
  (`severity=critcal`) used to return an empty list that looked like "no results".
  The request is still served as sent, with status **200** and the same items: no
  parameter is narrowed. When the value is outside the parameter's
  `x-hs-known-values`, the answer now also carries the optional body key
  `meta.warnings[]` (`param`, `value`, `known`) and the response header
  `X-HS-Unknown-Filter`, which names the parameter(s). Both are absent when
  every filter value is a published one, and the retired Spanish `severity`
  values inside their notice window raise no warning. `GET /v1/vendors`
  `category` is free text with no vocabulary and is not checked. Nothing
  existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-27 — correction: a scope needs its module active.** A tenant API key
  or a portfolio key was served on its scope alone, even when the tenant read no
  longer had that scope's module active; an OAuth access token already was not.
  Every credential now gets **403** with `error.details.code`
  `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`, `error.details.scopes` and `error.details.modules`
  (the module ids the tenant lacks) in that case (a new `error.details.code`
  value), plus `error.details.frameworks` when a compliance framework is
  entitled but not activated. A `compliance.<framework>` scope also needs
  the framework ACTIVATED for the tenant, not only included in its plan; an OAuth
  token no longer carries a compliance scope whose framework is not activated. **This changes what such a request receives:**
  it was a 200. `GET /v1/me` needs no scope and is unaffected. The same version
  adds the operation `listChanges` (`GET /v1/changes`, scope `changes:read`,
  read-only), the change-management register, served once at least one compliance
  framework is ACTIVATED for the tenant. Nothing else was removed, renamed or
  re-statused.

- **2026-10-26 — change: `user.email` on `GET /v1/me` needs the `email` scope.**
  The OAuth scope `email` is new. `user.email` is returned only to an access
  token that carries it, and is omitted otherwise: `user` still names the
  signed-in user by `id` and `name`. A client that shows the email asks for
  `email` at authorization; the consent screen lists it. The call is never refused
  for a missing `email` scope. A client that decoded `user.email` as required
  must treat it as optional.

- **2026-10-24 — correction: `beta` on `GET /v1/me` is the tenant's own.** For
  a client tenant of an MSSP whose own organisation is not in a running beta, `beta`
  is `active`, `running: true` and `ends_at: null` while the MSSP's beta runs
  (it is what lifts the client's access), and `null` otherwise: the MSSP's end date
  and whether its beta ended or converted are not the client's to read. The tenant's
  own organisation's beta is described as before. No field was added or removed.

- **2026-10-21 — addition: `user` on `GET /v1/me`.** The `whoAmI` answer gains
  a nullable `user` object (`id`, `name`, `email`): the signed-in user of an
  OAuth access token (`hs_at_…`), so a client can show who is logged in. It is the
  caller's own data only, never another user's. It is `null` for a tenant API key
  and for a portfolio key. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-20 — addition: `beta` on `GET /v1/me`.** The `whoAmI` answer gains
  a nullable `beta` object (`status`, `running`, `ends_at`): the beta of the
  tenant's own organisation, so a client can show when it ends. It is `null` for an
  organisation that never joined the beta and for a portfolio key; a beta inherited

code.description: Closed vocabulary; new members may be added (see Versioning).

message.description: For a human reading a log. Not stable; do not parse it.

details.description: Diagnostic, except `code` and the keys the operation’s error descriptions name, which are contract.

code.description: OPEN vocabulary (a value keeps its meaning and its HTTP status; new values may be added): `TENANT_HEADER_INVALID`, `TENANT_REQUIRED`, `TENANT_SELECTOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `UNKNOWN_QUERY_PARAMETER`, `BODY_NOT_JSON`, `BODY_TOO_LARGE`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`, `LICENCE_INACTIVE`, `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED`, `PLAN_WITHOUT_API`, `ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED`, `WRITE_ACTOR_UNRESOLVED`, `CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `OWN_PROPOSAL` (403), `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` (404), `REPORT_NOT_READY`, `FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `ALERT_RESOLVED`, `ALERT_STATE_CHANGED`, `DUPLICATE`, `OPEN_PROPOSAL_CAP`, `ACTIONS_PAUSED`, `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PROPOSAL_EXPIRED`, `ALREADY_DECIDED`, `NOT_DECIDABLE` (409).

scopes.description: With `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`: the scopes the credential carries whose module is not active for the tenant read.

modules.description: With `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`: the module ids the tenant read lacks, one per module, in the order of `scopes` (`supply_risk`, `compliance.nis2`, …; `compliance` for `changes:read`, which needs any activated compliance framework).

frameworks.description: With `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`, present only when it applies: the compliance framework ids (`nis2`, …) the tenant read is entitled to but has not activated.

deniedReason.description: With `PLAN_WITHOUT_API`: why the plan of the tenant read offers no API access. Today always `plan_without_api`.

bearerAuth.description: A tenant API key, created in the console under Settings → API keys with the minimum scopes it needs. Mandatory expiry (at most 365 days); it stops working as soon as the administrator who created it is removed from the tenant or loses the role, unless another administrator of the tenant takes it over.

portfolioKey.description: An MSSP portfolio key (`hsp_…`), created by an organisation administrator of an active managed security service provider in the console’s MSSP area (API keys). It lists the provider’s client tenants (`portfolio:read`) and reads ONE of them per request, selected with `X-HS-Tenant`, with the same data scopes a tenant API key uses. Read scopes, plus at most the two write scopes `alerts:write` (acknowledge and resolve an alert in the selected client) and `risks:write` (move a risk along its lifecycle there), each acting with the role, read on every request, of the provider user who created the key; mandatory expiry (at most 90 days); it stops working as soon as the administrator who created it is removed or loses the role; optional client subset and source IP ranges. Refused with 401 everywhere but `/v1`.

oauth2.description: A USER access token (`hs_at_…`) issued by the HodeiShield console, the OAuth 2.1 authorization server at `https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth` (metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` on its origin). Authorization code with PKCE (S256, mandatory) for applications with a browser; the RFC 8628 device authorization grant (`https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth/device/code`) for those without one. Every token is bound to ONE user and ONE tenant, chosen by the user on the consent screen, and carries read scopes only (and, for a token issued for the HodeiShield MCP server, `act:propose`; for a token of the HodeiShield CLI, `act:decide`, which decides proposals as the signed-in person); the tenant is re-checked against what the user can see on every request. Public clients register themselves (RFC 7591) at `/oauth2/register`; the HodeiShield CLI is pre-registered as `hodeishield-cli`. Revocation: RFC 7009 at `/oauth2/revoke`, or by the user in the console under Account → Application access.
